title: Meet Our Team
text:
Our lab brings together researchers with diverse backgrounds and expertise.





Alexander H. Hogan, MD, MS is Associate Professor of Pediatrics at UConn Health and Pediatric Hospitalist at Connecticut Children’s. He is a health-services researcher with a focus on equitably reducing pediatric respiratory morbidity. Over the last five years, he has spearheaded research projects exploring risk factors for pediatric asthma readmissions, health disparities during the COVID-19 pandemic, and the geographic clustering of bronchiolitis acute care in Connecticut. He is Research Director of the Pediatric Hospital Medicine fellowship and leads an NIH-funded K23 study on preventing RSV in Hartford communities. Dr. Hogan holds a BA from Williams College, an MD from Mount Sinai School of Medicine, and a Masters of Clinical Research Methods from Albert Einstein College of Medicine.







Molly Hagler is a Pediatric Hospital Medicine Fellow at Connecticut Children’s Medical Center in Hartford, CT. After completing medical school at the University of Tennessee Health Science Center, she attended residency at Le Bonheur Children’s Hospital in Memphis, TN. Dr. Hagler is passionate about medical education and is currently pursuing a Health Professions Education Online Graduate Certificate through the University of Connecticut. Her research interests include enhancing resident well-being and improving the patient experience within the teaching environment.

title: Research
text:
Our lab’s mission is to reduce pediatric morbidity and mortality using health services research and multi-center collaboration. Our work spans several key areas:




Through collaborations with the UConn GIS Health Lab at Connecticut Children’s we investigate the impact of place on pediatric health disparities.









Collaborating with Dr. Kimia’s NLP tool DrT to investigate predictors of Low Value Care in pediatrics.









Using PHIS and national datasets, we analyze trends in pediatric respiratory morbidity — with active projects on bronchiolitis geographic clustering, nirsevimab effectiveness (including an MMWR report across 24 states), and the impact of maternal RSV vaccination on pediatric hospitalizations.









We are developing a standardized clinical pathway for CHS management across ED and inpatient settings at Connecticut Children’s, paired with a retrospective chart review and multi-center database analysis.

title: Research
text: Through collaborations with the UConn GIS Health Lab at Connecticut Children’s we investigate the impact of place on pediatric health disparities. With a Hood Hub award (2026 to 2027), we are working with the Children’s Hospital Association and partner children’s hospitals to validate DeGAUSS, an open, privacy-preserving tool that links home addresses to neighborhood data, and to test whether it works equally well for every child. Recent work in the Journal of Pediatrics asked whether ZIP codes are good enough for measuring the Child Opportunity Index in pediatric hospitalization research.

title: Research
text:
Using PHIS and national datasets, we analyze trends in pediatric respiratory morbidity — with active projects on bronchiolitis geographic clustering, nirsevimab effectiveness (including an MMWR report across 24 states), and the impact of maternal RSV vaccination on pediatric hospitalizations. Our recent paper in Hospital Pediatrics describes bronchiolitis hospitalizations and cost at children’s hospitals in the era of RSV prevention.
With an NIH NIAID K23 award (2026), Preventing RSV: A Community-Engaged, Implementation Science Approach, we are learning from Hartford families why some newborns do not receive RSV immunization, co-designing a better way to offer it with parents and clinicians, and piloting it in a newborn nursery.

title: Our Mission & Values
text:
Our lab’s mission is to reduce pediatric morbidity and mortality using health services research (HSR) and community-engaged research (CEnR/CBPR) approaches.



Identifying modifiable factors that influence child health outcomes
Partnering with communities to develop effective interventions
Translating research findings into actionable policy recommendations
Building evidence for interventions that reduce health disparities

title: Our Mission & Values
text:
Vision
We envision a future where all children have the opportunity to thrive, regardless of their social or economic circumstances. We strive to be a leading research group that:

Bridges the gap between academic research and community needs
Develops innovative solutions to complex pediatric health challenges
Trains the next generation of health services researchers
Creates lasting positive change in pediatric healthcare delivery and outcomes

title: Our Mission & Values
text:
Core Values


Scientific Integrity

Commitment to rigorous, reproducible, and transparent scientific methods
Maintaining high standards for data quality and analysis
Supporting open science practices
Fostering a culture of continuous learning and improvement



Health Equity

Prioritizing research that addresses health disparities
Working to improve health outcomes for vulnerable patients
Reducing inequalities wherever possible
Ensuring our research benefits underserved communities



Inclusive Excellence

Recognizing valuable insights from all stakeholders
Ensuring all voices are heard and respected
Fostering a collaborative and supportive environment
Embracing diverse perspectives and experiences



Continuous Improvement

Adopting a process improvement mindset
Regularly evaluating and refining our methods
Being responsive to feedback from community partners
Supporting professional growth and development

title: Welcome to the Hogan Lab
text: We are excited to have you visit the Hogan Lab. We are a diverse group of clinicians, researchers, and trainees working to improve pediatric health outcomes through rigorous clinical and health services research.

title: Welcome to the Hogan Lab
text: We are excited to have you visit the Hogan Lab. We are a diverse group of clinicians, researchers, and trainees working to improve pediatric health outcomes through rigorous clinical and health services research.

title: Welcome to the Hogan Lab
text: Our work centers on pediatric respiratory illness — bronchiolitis, RSV, asthma, and emerging conditions such as Cannabis Hyperemesis Syndrome — using large national datasets, clinical trials, and multi-center collaborations to generate evidence that changes practice. Our newest work uses community-engaged implementation science to help more newborns receive RSV immunization, and open, privacy-preserving geocoding tools that other children’s hospitals can use.

title: Welcome to the Hogan Lab
text:
Our approach is methodologically diverse - we use whatever scientific methods are necessary to create rigorous, reproducible, and transparent research. As a member of our research community, you’ll find:

Large database and multi-center health services research
Prospective cohort and clinical trial design
Community-engaged, qualitative and implementation science methods
Geospatial methods that link where children live to how they do
Focus on pediatric respiratory and infectious disease outcomes
Commitment to translating findings into clinical practice

Learn more about our mission and values
